subject: Post-call recap: Tool-calling integration patterns & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Laura Chen <laura.chen@finapps.com>, Raj Patel <raj.patel@finapps.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 11 Aug 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: Tool-calling integration patterns & next steps

Hi Laura / Raj 

Thanks for the time today  great discovery call. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we can line up the architecture deep-dive with your engineering team.

Key takeaways from the call:
- Primary use case: in-app financial assistant that performs account lookups, transaction categorization, and assisted reconciliation.
- Expected load profile: bursty queries (primarily reads) with a mix of short conversational turns and occasional long-context retrieval flows.
- Security: SOC2 + SCIM provisioning are must-haves; data residency in us-west for initial rollout.
- Integration constraints: existing FinApps API is REST-based with API key auth today; team interested in Redwood tool/function-calling to orchestrate LLM->backend interactions.

Specific architecture questions we flagged that will shape the deep-dive agenda:
1) Auth & SDK setup: prefer a short-lived, service-account style credential for Redwood to call your protected endpoints (we support mTLS and signed JWT exchange). Can you confirm preferred auth pattern?
2) Tool definitions: we'll provide sample tool-definition JSON (input schema + response schema). Do you have an existing OpenAPI/contract we should map to, or prefer we propose a minimal wrapper?
3) Routing & fallbacks: do you want latency-sensitive calls routed to a low-latency path (read-only) vs heavier reconciliations routed to a batch worker?
4) Structured output & tool-calling: recommended approach is schema-validated tool responses (JSON) + an embeddings-based reranker for retrieved results.
5) Error handling: how should we surface transient backend errors to the model (to trigger a retry) vs permanent application errors?

Next steps (proposed):
- Tech deep-dive (60min) with your backend and security leads to walk through sample tool definitions, auth flow, and routing policies.
- We'll share a sample tool-definition bundle + integration diagram before the call.
- HubSpot deal touchpoint: plan to align on procurement timeline by the end of August.

Available times for our eng team this week: Wed 08/12 10:00-12:00 PDT, Thu 08/13 09:00-11:00 PDT. If those don't work, suggest alternatives and we'll coordinate.

Attachments: integration diagram (finapps-integration-diagram.png), sample tool definitions (sample-tool-definitions.json).

Best,

Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

Hi Marissa / team 

Thanks for the summary  this aligns well with what we discussed. A few clarifications from our side before the deep-dive:

1) Auth: we currently support API keys and OAuth 2.0 (client credentials). For server-to-server integrations we prefer OAuth client-credentials; we can also do an mTLS endpoint if needed. For the first pass, OAuth client-credentials + scoped roles should be sufficient.

2) API contract: attaching our current public API spec (abridged) and our security requirements doc (finapps-security-reqs.pdf). We do have an internal OpenAPI umbrella; happy to map specific endpoints you want the tool to call.

3) Tool expectations: would prefer a thin wrapper around our existing endpoints rather than a guess-at schema. If you can propose a minimal tool-definition that references our OpenAPI paths, that would speed things up.

4) Embeddings/reranker: we plan to send you a small sample dataset of returned transactions (for reranker tuning). Please confirm your embedding model recommendations and tokenization constraints.

Our engineering leads (Raj and I) can make Wed 08/12 10:30-11:30 PDT for a 60-minute deep-dive  that slot works for Raj and me.

Attachments: finapps-security-reqs.pdf, finapps-api-abridged.yaml

Thanks,

Laura Chen

laura.chen@finapps.com
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 12 Aug 2026 11:10:00 -07:00
Subject: FW: Post-call recap: Tool-calling integration patterns & next steps

Marissa / Michael 

Looping back with a quick internal plan before the deep-dive. I'm booking Raj/Laura for Wed 10:30-11:30 PDT as they suggested. Proposed Redwood attendees: Marissa (solutions), me (infra), Michael (security).

Draft tech agenda (60min):
- 00-05min: Intros + success criteria (Laura/Raj scope)
- 05-15min: FinApps API overview (Laura) + auth constraints
- 15-30min: Tool-definition proposal (Marissa): single-tool vs composite-tool, OpenAPI reference mapping
- 30-40min: Runtime routing & fallback patterns (Dylan): low-latency read path, async heavy work, canarying
- 40-50min: Structured output + schema validation + tool error semantics (Michael): transient vs permanent errors, retry windows
- 50-60min: Embeddings/reranker discussion + next steps (Marissa)

Notes on patterns to bring to the call:
1) Tool choice: recommend modeling each backend capability as a discrete tool when semantics are different (e.g., account_lookup, transaction_search, reconciliation_job). Composite tools (one tool that calls multiple endpoints) are OK for simple orchestration but increase coupling.
2) Parallel tools: for independent enrichment (e.g., fetch user prefs + fetch recent transactions) we can call tools in parallel and merge results server-side; we'll show guaranteed ordering vs best-effort merging strategies.
3) Error handling: include explicit error schema in tool responses  {"error_type":"TRANSIENT|PERMANENT","code":"...","message":"..."}  so the model or the runtime can decide retry vs surface. Also recommend idempotency tokens for any mutating calls.
4) Embeddings/rerankers: plan to prototype with a small evaluation set (send us 200 sample transactions). We'll recommend an embedding dimension and a candidate reranker approach (coarse filter with vector search, then LLM re-rank).

I'll attach the sample-tool-definitions.json to the deep-dive invite; Marissa, can you finalize the example wrapper by EOD?

Thanks,
Dylan

Thanks Laura  locking in Wed 08/12 10:30-11:30 PDT. Invite sent.

Attached is a short sample tool-definition bundle (sample-tool-definitions.json) that maps two primary tools to your OpenAPI paths:
- account_lookup: GET /v1/accounts/{account_id} -> returns schema: {account_id, balance, currency, last_updated}
- transaction_search: POST /v1/transactions/search -> accepts filters, returns list[transaction] with amount, date, merchant, category

Implementation notes (summary):
- SDK/Auth: we'll support OAuth client-credentials. We'll exchange a short-lived Redwood service token for calls to FinApps. If you prefer mTLS for production, Dylan's team can enable it.
- Routing: recommend routing read-only / low-latency tool calls to a warm thread on infra; heavier reconciliation starts an async job (reconciliation_job) with a job_id returned.
- Structured output: all tool outputs are JSON and validated against the tool schema before being surfaced to the LLM. We include an explicit error object in the response when something goes wrong.
- Parallel calls: by default we'll call independent enrichment tools in parallel and then apply a deterministic merge order; we can also expose a single combined tool if you'd rather hide parallelism.
- Embeddings/rerankers: we'll suggest a small pilot using a 1536-dim model (optimize for recall) + LLM re-rank for precision. We'll provide evaluation metrics (MRR/Precision@5).

Action items:
- FinApps: share the internal OpenAPI umbrella or point us to the exact endpoints you want in the pilot (Raj).
- Redwood: we'll send a short list of sample eval data requirements and the sample-tool-definitions.json (attached).
- Both: confirm procurement timeline  Laura, you mentioned procurement meeting late Aug; please share any constraints.

Drive link to pre-read + sample tool bundle: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1aB3k-example-drive-link

Thanks and talk soon 

Marissa Cole
